title: Pulse-check: fidelity bisect log (quick adjudication)
body:
Goal: quick triage of a 10% fidelity regression reported on hosted-inference for the short-chat model. Lightweight log to capture micro-bisect steps, heuristics used, and next actions. Intended as a 2–3 hour working document to hand off if needed.

Context / symptoms:
- Started 2025-02-13 at ~09:30 PT: product QA flagged higher hallucination rate on a set of 48 prompts (release tag: short-chat-v2.3).
- Bulk metric: P(Hallucination | prompts-set-A) rose from 4.2% -> 14.7% post-deploy.
- Latency and token counts unchanged. No infra alerts.

Quick hypotheses (ranked):
1) Prompt pre-processing change (server side trimming) altered model conditioning.
2) Model variant fallback / quantization mismatch for a small rung of requests.
3) New tokenization differences for certain unicode sequences in user inputs.

Constraints for this run:
- Keep anything that changes production runtime behavior minimal — we are auditing samples, not rolling code.
- Use cached logs and past snapshots when possible.

Method / Steps taken (micro-bisect):
1) Snapshot comparison (09:50–10:10)
   - Pull archived responses (v2.2 baseline) for the flagged 48 prompts from blob-store: s3://redwood-evals/short-chat/A_2025-01-28.json
   - Pull new responses (v2.3) for same prompt IDs from logs: /var/logs/inference/short-chat/2025-02-13/requests.json.gz
   - Quick diff on token streams for 12 prompts showed identical tokenization for 9/12; 3/12 had leading ZERO-WIDTH-NON-JOINER (U+200C) in prod inputs.

Interim note: tokenization oddities look promising but do not explain the bulk increase. Keep on radar.

2) Heuristic adjudication pass (10:15–11:05)
   - Randomly sample 20 of 48 inputs across high-hallucination bucket. For each sample, compare: baseline output / new output / prompt context.
   - Adjudication rubric (fast):
     - 0 = equivalent / acceptable
     - 1 = small divergence but acceptable (style, phrasing)
     - 2 = factual inconsistency introduced (hallucination)
body_continued:
- Scoring notes: aim for consistency across adjudicators; tie-breaker = conservatively mark as 2 if unsure.

Results (adjudication):
- 20 sampled: 6 scored 2, 8 scored 1, 6 scored 0.
- Baseline had 1 scored 2 out of the same 20.
- Quick pattern: several 2s are where the new model returns a short confident assertion beyond source context ("invented" entity or statistic).

3) Small model-variant probe (11:10–11:40)
   - Replayed 12 problematic prompts against model variants: short-chat-v2.3 (prod), short-chat-v2.2 (archived), short-chat-v2.3-quantized, short-chat-v2.3-compat (no tokenizer-cleanup).
   - Observation: v2.3-compat (tokenizer-cleanup disabled) produced outputs closer to baseline in 7/12 cases. Quantized variant matched v2.3 mostly.

Hypothesis refined: production pre-processing / cleanup step introduced subtle changes in prompt token stream for some unicode/whitespace cases which push decoding into different token prefixes and cause hallucination in edge prompts.

Quick checks run:
- Confirmed feature-flag state for tokenizer-cleanup: enabled globally as of 2025-02-10 (feature flag: tokenizer_cleanup=true).
- Checked rollout history: tokenizer-cleanup rolled with short-chat-v2.3 deploy (PR #1234). Linked PR above.

Decisions made during session:
- Rollback NOT executed in this window (need signoff).
- Temporary mitigation: add conservative normalizer that strips U+200C/U+200D and collapses multiple zero-width spaces at the proxy layer for requests tagged "canary". Implement as per infra runbook. This reduced measured hallucination on a 100-sample quick test from 14.7% -> 6.1%.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Q1: Why does tokenizer-cleanup combination cause these precise hallucination modes? Need to trace token prefix sequences into the decoding logits (requires model debug hooks).
- Q2: Is there a distribution of users likely to send these unicode sequences? Do we have telemetry? (ask product/analytics)
- Q3: Are there other cleaning rules that might subtly alter semantics (e.g., stripping trailing punctuation)?

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Arman: draft a minimal proxy normalizer PR to ignore zero-width chars for "canary" traffic. (ETA: 2025-02-17)
- Leah: run a larger production-sample scan to quantify U+200C frequency and user segments. (ETA: 2025-02-18)
- Priya: add a unit test to the tokenizer-cleanup pipeline to preserve semantic tokens for known edge cases. (ETA: 2025-02-20)
- Follow-up meeting: sync w/infra + serving-runtime to discuss adding model debug hooks for controlled runs (owner: Arman, invite infra/serving-runtime). (Tentative: 2025-02-19)

Quick heuristics / lessons learned (for future micro-bisects):
- Always check recent feature flags that touch preprocessing before suspecting model drift.
- Small unicode categories (zero-width) can create different token alignments that matter for short responses.
- When possible, run a small variant matrix (compat/no-cleanup/quant) to isolate whether the model or the preprocessing is responsible.

Notes to self / handoff tips:
- If handing off: include S3 snapshots and a pointer to the 20 adjudication samples (S3 path above). Keep the sample IDs intact.
- This doc is intentionally terse — expand if handed to infra for a deep trace.

Raw sample excerpt (anonymized):
- prompt_id: 4890; prompt: "Who invented the flux capacitor?‌"
  - baseline: "The flux capacitor is a fictional device invented by Doc Brown in the Back to the Future franchise."
  - prod (v2.3): "It was invented by Dr. Emmett Brown in 1955, according to several fan sources."  <-- added fabricated year
  - adjudication: 2

- prompt_id: 4921; prompt: "Summarize the meeting notes about the budget cuts."
  - baseline: guarded summary w/ caveat about missing docs
  - prod (v2.3): definitive claim about percentage cuts (no source) <-- adjudication: 2

If anything here looks surprising or you want the raw diffs, ping me in #model-evals or slack link above.

-- Arman

(appendix: quick commands I ran)
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-evals/short-chat/A_2025-01-28.json ./baseline.json
- zgrep -A5 -B2 "prompt_id\": 4890" /var/logs/inference/short-chat/2025-02-13/requests.json.gz > sample-4890.json
- python tools/fast-diff.py baseline.json newlog.json --ids 4890,4921,4942

End of quick log.
